question: Why do road safety vests worn by traffic officers at night have silver reflective strips on them?
options: They reflect light from car headlights into the driver's eyes, making the officer visible
They produce their own bright light continuously in total darkness
They absorb heat from car engines and glow in the dark
They bend car headlight rays away from the road
answer: They reflect light from car headlights into the driver's eyes, making the officer visible

question: How can a dentist inspect the back of a patient's upper tooth using a small angled mirror?
options: The mirror reflects light from the dental lamp off the back of the tooth into the dentist's eyes
The mirror produces its own light to shine on the dark tooth
The mirror bends light rays around the tooth so no shadow is formed
The mirror absorbs cold air from the patient's mouth
answer: The mirror reflects light from the dental lamp off the back of the tooth into the dentist's eyes

question: Why is frosted glass often used for bathroom windows instead of clear glass?
options: It is translucent, so it lets some light pass through while casting a faint shadow to block clear view
It is opaque, so it blocks all light and casts a very dark shadow
It is transparent, so it allows all light to pass through without casting any shadow
It acts as a light source to illuminate the bathroom automatically
answer: It is translucent, so it lets some light pass through while casting a faint shadow to block clear view

question: Ali tried to look at a lit candle through a flexible plastic hose bent into an S-shape. Why could he NOT see the flame?
options: Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through a bent hose
Plastic hose absorbs all light rays completely
Light turns into heat energy inside bent hoses
The candle flame stops glowing when viewed through plastic
answer: Light travels in straight lines and cannot pass through a bent hose

question: During a shadow puppet show, an actor wants a dragon puppet's shadow on the screen to become LARGER. What adjustment should he make?
options: Move the torch closer to the puppet
Move the puppet closer to the screen
Move the torch further away from the puppet
Move both the torch and screen further away
answer: Move the torch closer to the puppet

question: An unopened soup can is held between a light source and a screen. Depending on how it is held, which pair of shadow shapes can it cast?
options: A circle or a rectangle
A circle or a triangle
A square or a triangle
An oval or a square
answer: A circle or a rectangle

question: At 9:00 am, a vertical pole outdoors casts a long shadow pointing west. At 12:00 noon, how does the shadow compare?
options: The shadow is much shorter and positioned near the base of the pole
The shadow is much longer and points towards the east
The shadow stays the exact same length and position
The shadow turns into bright light because the Sun is overhead
answer: The shadow is much shorter and positioned near the base of the pole

question: A light sensor measures light passing through four material sheets: Sheet A (0 units), Sheet B (450 units), Sheet C (150 units), Sheet D (900 units). The torch gives off 900 units. Which sheet is OPAQUE?
options: Sheet A
Sheet B
Sheet C
Sheet D
answer: Sheet A

question: During a night football match, four large stadium lights shine on a player from four different directions. How many separate shadows will be cast on the field?
options: Four separate shadows because the player blocks light coming from four sources
Only one single black shadow directly beneath the player
No shadows because multiple lights cancel each other out
Two shadows because light rays merge in pairs
answer: Four separate shadows because the player blocks light coming from four sources

question: An opaque wooden card with a small square hole cut in its center is placed between a torch and a screen. What appears on the screen?
options: A dark rectangular shadow with a bright square patch in the middle
A bright background with a dark square shadow in the middle
A completely dark shadow with no light passing through
A dark square shadow with a bright circle in the middle
answer: A dark rectangular shadow with a bright square patch in the middle

question: Mei Ling wants to test if the DISTANCE between a light source and an object affects the height of its shadow. What is the ONLY variable she should change in her experiment?
options: The distance between the light source and the object
The height and shape of the object
The distance between the object and the screen
The brightness of the light source
answer: The distance between the light source and the object

question: A periscope uses two flat mirrors set at 45-degree angles inside a tube. How does a sailor inside a submarine view ships on the sea surface?
options: Light from the ship reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into his eyes
Light from his eyes shines out through both mirrors to illuminate the ship
Light bends continuously inside the tube without touching any mirrors
Light is absorbed by the top mirror and recreated by the bottom mirror
answer: Light from the ship reflects off the top mirror, then off the bottom mirror into his eyes

question: A chef uses a stainless steel frying pan with a wooden handle to cook. Why are stainless steel and wood chosen for these parts?
options: Stainless steel is a good conductor of heat so food cooks fast; wood is a poor conductor of heat so the chef's hand does not get burned
Stainless steel is a poor conductor of heat so food cooks slowly; wood is a good conductor of heat to warm the chef's hand
Both stainless steel and wood are good conductors of heat to speed up cooking
Both stainless steel and wood are poor conductors of heat to keep the kitchen cool
answer: Stainless steel is a good conductor of heat so food cooks fast; wood is a poor conductor of heat so the chef's hand does not get burned

question: An identical cold egg is added to Mug A (100 ml of hot water at 95°C) and Pot B (1000 ml of hot water at 95°C). Why does the egg cook faster and more thoroughly in Pot B?
options: Pot B contains a larger volume of water with more heat energy, so its temperature drops less when the cold egg is added
Pot B has a higher starting temperature than Mug A
Mug A absorbs coldness from the egg much faster
The larger volume of water in Pot B creates higher pressure on the egg
answer: Pot B contains a larger volume of water with more heat energy, so its temperature drops less when the cold egg is added

question: Cup 1 contains 100 ml of hot water at 90°C. Pot 2 contains 2000 ml of hot water at 90°C. Both are left on a table in a room at 25°C. Why does Cup 1 cool down to 25°C much faster than Pot 2?
options: Cup 1 contains a smaller volume of water with less heat energy, so it takes less time to lose its heat energy to the room
Cup 1 has a lower starting temperature than Pot 2
Pot 2 generates its own heat energy continuously while sitting in the room
Air in the room transfers coldness into Cup 1 faster than into Pot 2
answer: Cup 1 contains a smaller volume of water with less heat energy, so it takes less time to lose its heat energy to the room

question: A baker places a glass bowl of solid chocolate chips over a pot of hot water at 80°C. Why do the chocolate chips melt into a liquid?
options: The chocolate chips gain heat from the hotter water, causing their temperature to rise and melt
Coldness leaves the chocolate chips and enters the hot water
The glass bowl transfers coldness from the room into the chocolate
The hot water loses heat to the air, forcing the chocolate to melt
answer: The chocolate chips gain heat from the hotter water, causing their temperature to rise and melt

question: A cook inserts a digital temperature probe into the middle of a roasting turkey. What does the reading on the probe measure?
options: The degree of hotness of the turkey
The total amount of heat energy stored inside the entire turkey
The weight of heat transferred from the oven
The time needed for the turkey skin to turn brown
answer: The degree of hotness of the turkey

question: A boy drops two ice cubes at 0°C into a glass of hot lemon tea at 60°C. What happens to the heat energy and temperature of the tea?
options: Heat energy flows from the hot tea into the colder ice cubes; the temperature of the tea decreases
Coldness flows from the ice cubes into the hot tea; the temperature of the ice cubes increases
Heat energy flows from the ice cubes into the hot tea; the temperature of the tea increases
No heat flows because ice cubes do not contain heat energy
answer: Heat energy flows from the hot tea into the colder ice cubes; the temperature of the tea decreases

question: Mother finds it difficult to unscrew a tight metal lid on a glass jam jar. She runs hot water over the metal lid for 30 seconds, and the lid opens easily. Why?
options: The metal lid gains heat from the hot water and expands more than the glass jar
The glass jar gains heat from the hot water and contracts, releasing the lid
The metal lid loses heat to the hot water and shrinks, becoming looser
The hot water melts the glass jar rim so the metal lid slides off
answer: The metal lid gains heat from the hot water and expands more than the glass jar

question: Small gaps are intentionally left between concrete slabs on outdoor footpaths in Singapore. What is the main purpose of these gaps?
options: To allow space for the concrete slabs to expand when they gain heat on hot days without buckling
To allow space for the concrete slabs to contract when they gain heat on sunny days
To allow coldness to flow into the ground so the path stays cool
To prevent light from casting dark shadows under the footpath
answer: To allow space for the concrete slabs to expand when they gain heat on hot days without buckling

question: A baker wears thick cloth oven mitts when removing a hot metal tray at 180°C from the oven. Why do oven mitts protect his hands?
options: Cloth is a poor conductor of heat, so heat flows very slowly from the hot tray to his hands
Cloth is a good conductor of heat, so it absorbs all the heat energy from the tray instantly
Cloth transfers coldness from the air into his hands while holding the tray
Cloth stops the metal tray from expanding further inside his hands
answer: Cloth is a poor conductor of heat, so heat flows very slowly from the hot tray to his hands

question: While boiling water on a stove to cook soup, the water temperature reaches 100°C and stays at 100°C for 10 minutes while boiling continuously. Why does the temperature NOT rise above 100°C?
options: Water stays at its boiling point of 100°C while changing state into steam, even as heat is continuously supplied
The stove flame stops transferring heat energy once the water reaches 100°C
The water loses all its heat energy to the room at 100°C so no heat is gained
The thermometer stops recording temperature above 100°C
answer: Water stays at its boiling point of 100°C while changing state into steam, even as heat is continuously supplied

question: A chef uses a digital temperature sensor connected to a datalogger to monitor hot oil continuously while frying chicken. Why is this method preferred over using a glass thermometer?
options: It provides real-time, accurate digital readings safely without the risk of glass breaking in hot oil
It generates extra heat to make the oil reach 200°C faster
It prevents the cooking oil from gaining heat from the stove burner
It turns the hot oil into a poor conductor of heat
answer: It provides real-time, accurate digital readings safely without the risk of glass breaking in hot oil

question: A student poured 200 ml of hot coffee at 90°C into four cups made of different materials (W, X, Y, and Z). After 20 minutes in a room at 25°C, the temperatures were recorded: Cup W = 75°C, Cup X = 50°C, Cup Y = 62°C, and Cup Z = 40°C. Which material is MOST suitable for making a mug to keep cold coffee cool for the longest time?
options: Material W, because its coffee had the highest remaining temperature, showing it is a poor conductor of heat that lost heat slowest
Material Z, because its coffee dropped to 40°C, showing it gained coldness fastest
Material X, because a middle temperature of 50°C shows it is a good conductor of heat
Material Y, because its coffee cooled down faster than Cup W
answer: Material W, because its coffee had the highest remaining temperature, showing it is a poor conductor of heat that lost heat slowest so it will also gain heat the slowest
